newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian forward dlr may dip further, spot dlr firm.
newsitem.headline: Indian forward dlr may dip further, spot dlr firm.

text.p: Forward premia dipped below 7.0 percent for April dollars on Wednesday, down from Tuesday's close of 7.07 percent, dealers said.
"Corporates were receiving even today," said a bank dealer, referring to firms selling their forward dollar receivables.
"Forwards still show signs of moving down further," said Moses Harding, chief forex dealer at IndusInd Bank in Bombay.
"I see the momentum of receiving (of premia) slowing down," said a dealer. He expected some support at 7.0 percent.
He agreed the six-month premium could dip further, but said there was no way premium would fall below six percent.
In the spot market, sustained dollar selling continued and Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought dollars around the closing rate of 35.5950/6000, arresting the rupee's rise, dealers said.
One banker said there was a lurking suspicion that there could be some pressure on the government to push the rupee down after neighbouring Pakistan devalued its rupee on Wednesday.
"The difference (between Pakistani and Indian rupee) is now almost five rupees," said a dealer. "And they are our competitor in many commodities," he said.
